questions.q: What is the environment? Describe its major components.
answer: The environment is our surroundings — everything, living and non-living, around us that affects life. It has natural, human and human-made components interacting together.

answer.text: This has four domains: the lithosphere, the solid land or crust; the hydrosphere, all the water in oceans, rivers and lakes; the atmosphere, the blanket of air; and the biosphere, the narrow zone where land, water and air meet and support life.
The human environment is people, their activities and society, while the human-made environment is what people build — houses, roads, dams and cities.

answer: These components constantly interact, and humans must use and modify the natural environment carefully to keep it healthy.

questions.q: What is an ecosystem? Explain why its parts are interdependent.
answer: An ecosystem is a community of living organisms interacting with the non-living, physical environment around them.

answer.text: A forest, a pond and a desert are all ecosystems, each with its own plants, animals and physical conditions such as soil, water and climate.

The living and non-living parts depend on one another. Plants need sunlight, air, water and soil; animals depend on plants and on one another for food; and when they die, they return nutrients to the soil. Because everything is linked, disturbing one part — for example cutting down trees — affects the whole ecosystem.

answer: This is why ecosystems must be protected and used with care.
